rationale: The question is how well an existing score separates residents who will leave from those who will stay, which is a diagnostic (prognostic) accuracy question: one index test, one pre-specified cut-off, one reference standard ascertained blind to the score. Every resident who completes the month-3 seminar is tested, and separation dates are complete in human resources records (c2). The retrieved accuracy estimate (c1) is a planning value, and predictive values must be measured at the local separation rate (c3). Reporting follows STARD 2015.
alternatives: Prediction model with several predictors (refused: about 56 expected separations cannot support more than two or three predictors)
Stated intention to leave as the trigger (refused as the sole trigger: it misses about half of leavers, claim c4)
Offer the booster to every resident without screening (kept as the fallback if accuracy is poor)
whyNotMoreComplex: A multivariable model or a trial of the booster would need more separations and a validated trigger first; a single accuracy estimate at a fixed cut-off answers the question the booster plan depends on.

decision.statement: Run a diagnostic accuracy study of the month-3 Transition Check at a pre-specified cut-off of 30 or below against separation from the hospital within 12 months of hire, in the four intakes from October 2026 to October 2027, before any mentoring booster is tied to the score.
decision.question: Does a month-3 Transition Check score of 30 or below identify new graduate nurses who separate within 12 months of hire accurately enough to target a mentoring booster?

criteria.text: A comparable self-rating showed useful but imperfect accuracy elsewhere and predictive values depend on the local separation rate, so local accuracy has to be measured.
The residency changes the timing or content of the month-3 seminar during the study period.

gates.requirement: Research ethics board approval of the residency evaluation protocol
gates.evidence: Approval REB-2026-417 dated 2026-07-30, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Human resources release of hire and separation dates prepared blind to the scores
gates.evidence: Data release memorandum HR-DR-2026-12 signed 2026-08-12, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Offer the booster to every resident without screening
Use stated intention to leave at month 6 as the trigger
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3, each from a retrieved record, and on the investigator's approval records for both gates.

summary: Diagnostic accuracy study recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims from retrieved records and both gates are met on investigator-supplied approvals.
